chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both)

about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Indeed, We presented the trust upon the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to carry it and feared it, and the human being carried it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.'
So he said: The trust is the Divine Authority (Wilayah); he who proclaims it without right, has disbelieved.

key_terms.الْأَمَانَةُ: The Trust (specifically identified as Wilayah in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'Trust' (Amanah) in Surah Al-Ahzab according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) offers a definitive Shia exegesis of the 'Trust' in Surah Al-Ahzab, identifying it specifically as *Wilayah* (Divine Authority) rather than a general moral duty. This interpretation anchors the cosmic refusal of the heavens and earth in the political-spiritual reality of Imamate, establishing that claiming this divine mandate without rightful succession constitutes *Kufr*. It underscores the centrality of *Wilayah* as the core covenant of faith in Shia theology.
